full_details: The night before the drawing was the worst of them. You paced with oil of cloves on the gum. Your head went to the constable at Grendon, to the cloth-workers' old arguments, and to Golding's lovers at a wall, and then to one solemn figure with an ass's head. You laughed into the shawl until the jaw stopped you. You wrote one word on the tables, weaver, and you do not yet know what it is for. At ten you sat a joined stool at Bishopsgate. A boy held your shoulders. Yaxley told you to hold the stool and think on your sins. You got as far as the second sin. He showed you three roots like a small black claw, and you would not keep the tooth. The price was twelve pence. You walked home with a clout on the jaw. Mistress Ansell had broth ready and had forbidden the stair. Alse went up once with salt water. At dusk you said the tyrant was gone, and no bigger than a pea. You entered twelve pence to the barber, and you did not write a balance under it.
one_sentence: Before dawn you wrote the word weaver, and at ten Yaxley drew the tooth on a joined stool for twelve pence.
title: Had the tooth drawn, and wrote weaver
